text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

The panel's composition proves nothing. All-women panels occur routinely by chance in many departments, and there's no evidence panels favour candidates of their own sex. Raising it makes you look aggrieved rather than wronged, and it's the weakest card you hold.

Your strong card is substantive: a completed PhD versus an unfinished one, six papers versus two, four years' teaching for a teaching post. Ask what criteria were weighted and how "industry experience" was scored against them.

Note the real possibility that industry links were genuinely decisive, or valued more than you'd expect.

Send a written follow-up citing your right to a reasoned decision, with a deadline. If the criteria turn out to be incoherent or shifting, escalate then.
